materials.where: door
inside of top block, plus 2 locally on flanges
1 in strip over the cut edges

completion: Four BID plies laid over release film
0.7 in flange marked and the top block cut off
One BID ply inside, plus two locally
Reflox with a 1 in BID strip; ten flush screws and nutplates

ops.title: Shock strut (optional)
ops.summary: Optional. For rough or grass fields, fit the spring assembly in place of the NG9 or NG10A rod; the Roncz text assumes it is fitted.

changes.note: For rough fields, a spring assembly replaces the NG9 and NG10A rod.

completion: Decision made: rod, or spring assembly for rough fields
Spring assembly in place of NG9/NG10A (CP25 LPC 27)

ops.title: Firewall accessory parts
ops.summary: Make the belcrank plates, brackets, pulley brackets, brake arms and the bushing from the printed patterns. Most come prefabricated.
completion: CS15 (2), CS71 (4), CS72 (2), BA (2), CS75 and the CS73 brackets made or bought
No model of these small parts yet; the later steps show only the assembled hardware

ops.title: Stainless firewall sheet
ops.summary: Trial-fit the stainless sheet over the engine-mount angles and the six studs. Caulk a bead of silicone near the edge, press the sheet on, bolt the pulley brackets, clamp it and cure two days. Fit the insulation after the cowling.

changes.note: Aluminium may replace the stainless sheet; insulation waits until after the cowling is fitted, using silicone rubber.
Move the left rudder pulley bracket up 0.6 in to keep the cable off the aileron pushrod, or bend it so the pulley sits about 0.2 in aft.

completion: Sheet trial-fitted over the extrusions and six studs
Silicone bead about 1/8 in, an inch from the edge; sheet pressed on and clamped top and bottom
Pulley brackets bolted, three
Insulation deferred until after the cowling, per the newsletter

ops.title: Rudder belcrank brackets
ops.summary: Offset the rudder and brake belcrank from the cable slot, drill through the stainless, insulation and plywood, and bolt it with AN3 bolts. Inboard nuts sit in the baggage space; outboard nuts are reached through a ground hole.
completion: Belcrank assembly offset from the cable slot
Holes (#10) drilled through stainless, insulation and ply; AN3-6A bolts fitted
Outboard nut access hole filled afterwards with dry micro
Belcrank height on the firewall is read from tick marks only (representational)

ops.title: Brake master cylinders
ops.summary: Mount Cleveland or Gerdes master cylinders upright between the engine-mount fittings. Bolt the lower bracket flush, fit the upper brake arm free to move, and use a longer bolt later with the engine mount.
completion: Cylinders upright between the upper and lower engine-mount fittings
Lower CS73 bracket drilled and countersunk for flush AN509 screws
Upper brake arm on CS75, free to move
Cylinder positions are not printed (representational)

ops.title: Right-hand consoles
ops.summary: Build the right front and rear consoles from thin foam, glass them inside, and bond them to the side, bulkheads and panel. Leave a large stick opening in the front console.

materials.where: inside of each console
outside of each console, 1/2 in lap

completion: Foam consoles cut and glassed inside with one BID ply
Bonded to the side, bulkheads and panel with micro
Two BID plies outside with a 1/2 in lap
Stick opening left in the front console; console shapes are fitted (representational)

ops.title: Stick pivot bulkheads
ops.summary: Flox the CS109 front and CS118 rear plywood pivot bulkheads to the consoles and sides, then glass round them.

materials.where: round CS109 and CS118 pivot bulkheads

completion: CS109 and CS118 bonded with flox
Two BID plies all round each
Pivot planes at FS 45.5 and FS 89.7 (medium confidence, read from leaders)

ops.title: Firewall torque-tube bearing
ops.summary: Cut a one-inch hole through the firewall right of centre and dimple the flanged bronze bearing so flox can grip it. Do not flox it yet; the torque tube goes in first.
completion: 1 in hole at BL 6.2 right, WL 12.3
Flanged bronze bearing dimpled in eight places with a 1/4 drill, not drilled through
Bearing left unfloxed until the torque tube is through the firewall (next step)

ops.title: Torque tubes
ops.summary: Build the tube inserts, pilot-drill both stick pivots in one plane, ream the press fit, and run the tube through the firewall. Fit the phenolic bearings and bolt them to the pivot bulkheads.

changes.note: Open the pivot holes with a letter U drill, then a 3/8 press-fit reamer, for a better interference fit.
The CS120 universal joint is MS20271-B10, not AN271-B10.

completion: CS105, CS106, CS115 and CS112 inserts built
Both stick pivots drilled in one plane; press fit reamed
Tube installed through the firewall; CS108 and CS117 bearings bolted to CS109 and CS118
CS120 on CS121, then the CS123 bearing floxed into the firewall hole with the tube in place; left undisturbed to cure

ops.title: Sticks and roll pushrod
ops.summary: Fit the front and rear sticks on tight bolts and make a pushrod so both stay parallel. Hold the sticks 5 degrees inboard, drill the torque-tube link, fit rod ends and grease the five pivots.

changes.note: The CS119 tube is 4.1 in long, not 3.1 in.
The jam nut shown is not in the bill of materials; a tapped MS21042-3 nut will do.

completion: CS103 front and CS119 rear sticks on tight 1/4 bolts
CS110 fitted so both sticks stay parallel
Sticks 5 degrees inboard when the link to CS120 is drilled
Rod-end thread depth checked; five pivots greased
Stick fore-aft positions are not printed (representational)

ops.title: Pitch pushrod
ops.summary: Make the two-piece pitch pushrod with rod ends and a quick disconnect. On the Roncz canard one extra 0.4 in spacer offsets the elevator-end rod end outboard.
completion: CS102 and CS136 pushrods made with HM4 ends and the quick disconnect
One extra 0.4 in CS-202 spacer at the elevator-end rod end (Roncz only)
Elevator travel on the Roncz canard is 15 degrees up and 30 down; no pitch stop is printed in the plans

ops.title: Aileron linkage (after the wing)
ops.summary: This waits on the wing from chapter 19. Join the stick to the aileron with the two 90-degree angles held, ailerons neutral, and protect the rod-end threads.
completion: Wing built and in place (chapter 19, not in this graph)
CS125L and CS126L joined by quick disconnects
Both 90-degree angles held with ailerons neutral; rod-end threads not bent

ops.title: Rudder cable conduits
ops.summary: Run two long nylon conduits along the sides at WL 8, through the four bulkhead holes, floxed at intervals. Thimble a cable to CS15 and slot the firewall.
completion: Two 82 in nylon conduits at WL 8 through the four bulkhead holes
Flox about every 6 in; conduits pass over the brake LB17 block
3/32 cable thimbled to CS15; firewall slotted

ops.title: Rudder cable rigging (after the winglet)
ops.summary: This waits on the winglet from chapter 20. With the pedal vertical at full rudder, set the sleeve 0.7 in off the firewall, run the pulley and 1/16 cable, and set the rudder travel with 0.7 in of overtravel at each end.
completion: Winglet and rudder built and in place (chapter 20, not in this graph)
CS15 sleeve 0.7 in off the firewall with the pedal vertical at full rudder
Rudder top trailing edge about 6 in out (30 degrees), wedge fitted, cable swaged
0.7 in overtravel at both ends

ops.title: Brake cables
ops.summary: Run 3/32 cable from CS15 to the master cylinder arm with a rubber sleeve, slack until full rudder. The cylinder acts as the rudder stop. Check it returns smoothly.
completion: Cable from CS15 to the master cylinder arm with rubber sleeve
Slack until full rudder is reached
Pedals return smoothly

ops.title: Adjustable pedals (optional)
ops.summary: Optional adjustable pedal hardware, positioned about 8 in forward of the panel.
completion: Optional hardware fitted about 8 in forward of the panel
Pedal travel still checked against the rudder cable rig

ops.title: Trim mount blocks
ops.summary: Make the two birch mounting blocks, bond the pitch-trim one to the left side, and notch the right console and bond the roll-trim one there, each with a BID ply over it.

materials.where: over PT1 on the left fuselage side, 1/2 in lap
over RT3 on the right console and side, 1/2 in lap

completion: PT1 and RT3 cut from 1/4 birch
Skin dremelled for the AN3 bolts; PT1 floxed to the left side, one BID ply over
Right console notched 1/4 by 1 in; RT3 bonded, one BID ply over

ops.title: Trim parts and springs
ops.summary: Make the pitch handle, the roll-trim levers and the phenolic washers, and cut the springs to their free lengths.
completion: PTH, RT1, two RT2 and four PW made
Springs cut to free length: PTS 6.0 in, RTS 2.0 in, CS 0.5 in

ops.title: Pitch trim
ops.summary: Swage two cables to the pitch handle, set them with the trim neutral, and spring the handle to the elevator belcrank. On the Roncz canard that belcrank is the NC-5A on the left tube. Set the friction and cut the slot.
completion: Two 20 in cables swaged to the handle, nylon sleeves in the panel holes
Swages set with neutral trim, 5.6 and 6.2 in from the panel sleeve
PTS springs to the NC-5A on the left tube (about BL 9.2 left, medium confidence), safety-wired
Elevator at zero at neutral trim; friction set and slot cut
Handle fore-aft station is a conflict in the plans, so none is stated here

ops.title: Roll trim
ops.summary: Sew the roll springs to their levers, bolt two levers to the stick torque tube, and mount the third on its block with friction hardware. The friction should just hold full right trim against full left stick.
completion: RTS springs sewn to RT2 and RT1
Two RT2 levers bolted on CS105; RT1 on RT3 with friction hardware
Friction holds full right trim against full left stick
Slot left for the cosmetic cover (chapter 24)

ops.title: Fixed trim tab (optional)
ops.summary: Only if shortening the pitch spring is not enough, add a small aluminium tab on the elevator.
completion: Tab of 1.2 by 10 by 0.02 in aluminium fitted only if needed
Left out if shortening the spring already centres the trim
